title: Adaptive dashboard canvas and interactive rollout timeline components
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a set of reusable design components and token mappings for the Redwood Console dashboard canvas and a tightly integrated interactive rollout timeline. Goals: 1) create an adaptive canvas system that supports multi-column metric cards, live data rails, and editorial panels across three density modes (compact / default / spacious); 2) design an interactive rollout timeline component used in feature rollouts and canary experiments that supports scrub, pinch-to-zoom, annotations, and linked metric snapshots; 3) define token-level mappings (spacing, elevation, type scale, color semantics) so engineering can derive CSS variables and Figma tokens consistently for private and hosted console variants. This ticket bundles prototypes, accessibility requirements, motion choreography, and handoff assets for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas supports 1-4 column layouts and gracefully collapses at defined breakpoints (<=640px, 641-1024px, >1024px)
Metric cards and panels have documented token mappings for spacing, elevation, and color states and export-ready Figma tokens
Rollout timeline supports keyboard scrubbing (arrow keys), range selection (shift+arrow), and screen-reader friendly labels for time slices
Performance-conscious motion: micro-interactions <120ms, scrubbing does not re-render expensive charts while dragging (use snapshot proxy)
Design QA checklist completed and signed off by Eng, PM, and Accessibility lead
Prototype links (Figma) include annotated flows for first-render loading, empty states, partial data, and error states
notes: Design trade-offs: to meet latency and rerender constraints, timeline scrub will show pinned lightweight snapshots instead of live charts while dragging; full charts refresh on drop
Token decisions: prefer semantic token names (e.g., token.surface.elev-1) over component-specific tokens; map component variants to semantic tokens in Figma
Accessibility: time markers must expose aria-valuenow/valuetext; ensure 4.5:1 contrast for all actionable elements in compact density
Edge cases: very long rollout windows (>90 days) should fall back to summarized ticks and allow zooming to day/hour resolution
Integration notes for Eng: provide spec for skeleton states and guidelines for incremental hydration when charts stream data
Localization: timeline labels need space for long locale strings; include ellipsis rules and tooltip fallback
